name: Marovo Lagoon
blurb: Seagrass, reef and mangroves in a huge double-barrier lagoon.

tip.title: Remove the tiger sharks
tip.text: Tiger sharks hunt green turtles and dugongs. Set Tiger shark to -100% and watch turtles and dugongs, then the seagrass and algae they graze.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong equatorial sun powers the seagrass, algae and corals of the shallow lagoon and the rainforest on the islands.
Frequent rain feeds the island forest and sends fresh water and sediment down to mangroves and the lagoon.
Bacteria, fungi and small invertebrates break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the mud and water.

nodes.name: Mangrove
nodes.desc: A mangrove tree of tidal shores in the western Pacific, recorded near the lagoon. Mangrove stands shelter the shoreline and young animals.
Small seagrasses of shallow sandy lagoon floors. Dugongs and green turtles graze seagrass meadows.
Calcified green algae and other algae growing on reef flats and rock. They feed parrotfish, surgeonfish and green turtles.
Rainforest figs bear fruit that is eaten by fruit bats and fruit pigeons. Weeping fig was among the plants recorded near the lagoon.
Reef fish that graze algae off rock and coral. Blacktip reef sharks and many fish-eating birds eat such reef fish.
Reef fish that scrape algae from rock with strong beaks. Their grazing keeps algae from smothering reef structure and makes sand.
Adults graze seagrass and algae in shallow lagoons. Tiger sharks are their main predator.
A marine mammal that eats mainly seagrass, often whole plants. Its grazing and digging reshape seagrass beds.
A shoreline wader of reefs and rocky coasts, frequently recorded near the lagoon. It hunts small fish and crustaceans in shallows.
A fish-eating raptor that dives for prey in shallow water. Recorded around the lagoon.
A coastal raptor that takes fish and other small prey and also feeds on dead animals along the shore.
A shark of shallow reefs and sand flats that eats small reef fish such as surgeonfish. Tiger sharks sometimes prey on it.
An ambush apex predator of mangroves, estuaries and coasts. Its range includes the Solomon Islands, and it takes fish, birds, crabs and sharks.
An open-water predator that hunts turtles of all sizes and also eats other sharks. The main natural predator of green turtles.
